ranking.note: Base of the chain: crash hardening that #29409 and thus #10102 depend on; reviewing it first unblocks the rest.
Largest benefit in the category but gated on #36520/#29409, so placed just behind its prerequisites.
Raised within band: fixes concrete shutdown races/crashes in IPC, same class of consequence as the other reliability fixes, ahead of feature work.
Raised within band: a documented data race (#36515) in the mining IPC path outranks additive interface features.
Raised within band: the installed wrapper fails outright on common distro layouts, a user-visible breakage rather than new capability.
Lowered within band: valuable but entirely gated on #10102/#29409, so it sits behind the reliability and platform fixes that are reviewable now.
Lowered within band: single unique commit stacked on #10102 and #19460; cannot be acted on before them.

inconsistencies: Dependency chain that must be reviewed in order: #36520 -> #29409 -> #10102 -> #19460 -> #19461. The leaf PRs (#19460, #19461) cannot merge until the base lands, so reviewer effort should start at #36520.

#35932 and #36572 both address event-loop/connection teardown races in the IPC layer and both touch libmultiprocess; review #35932 first (it has reproduced node crashes from #35845/#33387) and check #36572 for overlap or conflict with its subtree bump.
#32387, #36097 and #35932 each carry or depend on libmultiprocess subtree updates; whichever lands first will force the others to rebase their subtree commits.

#36525 and #36097 both make breaking changes to the mining IPC interface (Block handle vs. cancellation arguments); they should be sequenced deliberately so external clients like sv2-tp face one break, not two.
#36525 and #33922 both touch block-template lifetime/BlockTemplateManager bookkeeping; #36525's data-race fix should be reviewed before #33922's accounting feature builds on the same structures.

#32387 adds Windows IPC support and #36190 tests Windows wrapper exit-status behaviour; #36190 is a follow-up to already-merged wrapper work but overlaps the same surface, so #32387 should be reviewed first.
result.notes: The band spread is justified: four PRs form the project's crash-safety and enablement core (P1), a broad P2 middle of reliability fixes, platform coverage and interface features, and a small P3/P4 tail of tests and narrow parsing fixes. #36753 is only partly in scope (JSON-RPC error reporting) but is kept here because the defect was found auditing the IPC interface and shows up via bitcoin-cli over IPC.
